fragment_A.why: R3: an unresolved capture is itself a FAIL. Evaluation halts at ordering step 5, and the halt is recorded — unlike case 007, where assertions went missing unrecorded.

assertions.text: log(orders).line where trace_id == {{TRACE_ID}} within single_hop count >= 1

harness_findings.detail: The issued selector does not contain the declared correlator, and the capture it depends on is empty. The three matched lines are not provably this execution's.

fragment_B.why: The recorded result: true is not honored. This is the case: a conformant evaluator returns FAIL while every assertion in the bundle says true, because the evidence is not attributable to this execution.

fragment_C.why: The assertion is not false — it is unevaluatable. Returning FAIL would point the reader at the product; the defect is in the specification, which captured the array instead of its length. Note that the actual value 2 would have made a coincidental PASS very easy to reach by coercion.

conformance_note: Fragment B is the load-bearing one. An evaluator that returns PASS for it will return PASS for the single most common way an agent-executed suite goes wrong. Fragment C checks that INDETERMINATE is reached from the closed list by computation, not used as a residual category — an evaluator that coerces the array to its length and returns PASS is non-conformant.
